title: Project Overview and Pipeline
description: README.txt is the run guide and the closest thing this project has to an entry point. It describes one three-stage pipeline used for every experiment: train a GPT, train VQ-VAEs on the GPT's hidden states, then compute mutual information (MI) between the learned discrete codes. The same pipeline runs on four task families (CFG, short and long path finding, and OpenWebText), each with a next-token (NTP) and a multi-token (MTP/'mtl') variant. Keep this train, quantize, measure loop in mind for the rest of the tour.

title: Synthetic CFG Datasets
description: The first task family is a synthetic hierarchical context-free grammar. CFG_data_generation.py defines the grammar class, which samples random production rules, generates sequences in parallel and checks them with a fast parser. The full-sequence and prefix scripts load a pickled grammar instance and write padded binary corpora with BOS tokens. Because the grammar is known exactly, later steps can check whether model completions are valid.
languageLesson: Python's pickle module serializes whole objects, so the generated grammar, with its rules and methods, can be saved once and reloaded by the other scripts. This keeps every dataset split consistent with the same grammar.

title: Path-Finding Graph Datasets
description: The second task family is path finding on random tree-like graphs that contain correct paths and decoy paths. path_finding_generate_multi_cpu.py splits generation across worker processes that write temporary JSONL files, then merges them into the final splits. Each split (train, val, vqvae, mi, and so on) has its own JSON config. For example, the PF_15XL train config produces 16M samples with up to 28 nodes, 2 paths and 2 decoys. This generator has one of the highest fan-ins in the graph, because many configs and downstream scripts depend on it.
languageLesson: JSONL (JSON Lines) stores one JSON record per line. Parallel workers can each write their own file and the results can be merged by simple concatenation. A reader can also stream the records one at a time instead of loading the whole dataset.

title: OpenWebText Natural Language
description: The third task family uses real text. prepare.py downloads OpenWebText through HuggingFace datasets, tokenizes it in parallel with the GPT-2 BPE tokenizer from tiktoken, and writes train.bin and val.bin as flat uint16 token arrays. The readme next to it records the output size: about 9B training tokens. Compared with the synthetic CFG and path tasks from Steps 2-3, this tests whether the analysis still holds on natural language.
languageLesson: numpy.memmap maps a binary file on disk straight into an array, so training scripts can take random slices of a multi-gigabyte token file without loading all of it into RAM. uint16 is enough here because GPT-2's vocabulary (50257) is smaller than 65536.

title: Transformer Building Blocks
description: With the datasets covered, the tour moves to the model library. modules.py provides the basic pieces: LayerNorm, rotary positional embeddings, rotary self-attention with flash-attention support, an MLP and a TransformerBlock. These blocks are reused by the VQ-VAE encoders and decoders later on, so the same attention mechanism appears both in the GPT and in the models that compress the GPT's hidden states.
languageLesson: Rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) encode position by rotating query and key vectors by a position-dependent angle. Attention scores then depend on the relative distance between tokens, and no learned position table is needed.

title: The GPT Model
description: model.py is the GPT that every experiment trains. Along with the usual rotary-attention transformer, it has multi-token-prediction (mtl) heads and losses, generation with EOS handling, and APIs for extracting hidden states. That last feature connects the stages: the VQ-VAE and MI scripts call into a trained GPT to read its internal representations. model.py and minimal_VQVAEs.py have the highest fan-in in the project.
languageLesson: Multi-token prediction adds extra output heads that predict tokens t+2, t+3, ... in addition to t+1. With 'shared heads', most parameters are reused across offsets. The extra loss terms push the hidden state to encode information about the future, which is the effect this project measures.

title: Training GPTs on CFG
description: llm_train.py is the first runnable script in the README workflow. It trains the GPT from Step 6 on the CFG data from Step 2, using next-token or multi-token targets, with DDP support and periodic accuracy checks. llm_train_utils.py supplies the cosine LR schedule with warmup, metadata export, and a parallel check of whether model completions are valid under the grammar. Each experiment directory holds a Python config. The mtl4 variant shown here enables shared-head MTL with mtl_length=4 on the same dataset as the NTP baseline.
languageLesson: These nanoGPT-style configs are plain Python files whose top-level variables are executed into the training script's globals, overriding the defaults. That is why switching from NTP to MTP only requires pointing at a different config file.

title: Path-Finding and NLP Training
description: The same GPT is trained on the other two task families. path_finding_llm_train.py uses PathFindingDataset from path_finding_llm_utilities.py, which builds a vocabulary from the JSONL graphs of Step 3, tokenizes edges and paths, and can mask the loss on edge tokens. It also reports path accuracy. NLP_llm_train.py trains on the memmapped OpenWebText bins from Step 4 with mixed precision and gradient accumulation, configured by configGPT3Xsmall.py (an 8-layer, 512-dim GPT).
languageLesson: PyTorch's DistributedSampler gives each DDP process a disjoint shard of the Dataset. That is why the path-finding script uses a DataLoader-based dataset, while the OpenWebText script samples random windows directly from a memmap.

title: VQ-VAE Model Library
description: The second stage compresses GPT hidden states into discrete codes. minimal_VQVAEs.py defines many VQ-VAE variants (single, two-stage, layer/block, last-token, path, 3v2, 61) with encoders and decoders built from the modules.py blocks of Step 5. It also tracks codebook usage and includes cosine-push and soft-entropy regularizers. vqvae_utils.py is the shared helper library: optimizer, LR and beta schedules, masked NRMSE reconstruction metrics, and a wrapper that loads a trained GPT checkpoint and extracts its hidden states.
languageLesson: A VQ-VAE replaces each continuous encoder output with the nearest vector in a learned codebook. Gradients pass through the non-differentiable lookup with the straight-through estimator, and a commitment loss weighted by beta keeps encoder outputs close to their chosen codes.

title: Training VQ-VAEs on CFG
description: These scripts apply the VQ-VAE library to a frozen CFG GPT from Step 7. train_minimal_vqvae1.py trains the first-stage, layer-wise VQVAE1. train_minimal_vqvae2.py then loads that frozen VQVAE1 and trains VQVAE2 on its normalized outputs, forming a two-stage hierarchy. train_minimal_vqvae_single.py trains a single-representation baseline. Each run is configured by a JSON file in the experiment folder that sets codebook size, iteration count and output directory.

title: Path and NLP VQ-VAE Variants
description: The other tasks need VQ-VAEs tailored to their structure. On path finding, path_finding_vqvae61_train.py trains VQVAE61, which encodes hidden representations across several time steps for the long task. path_vqvae_train.py learns codes directly over the path token sequences, giving the target variable that MI is measured against. For OpenWebText, NLP_vqvae_layer_and_block_train.py quantizes hidden states per layer or per block of layers, and the matching layer_and_block config sets T=256.

title: Information-Theory Toolkit
description: Before the final stage, the tour covers the math it uses. information_theory_utils.py provides StreamingInfo, a count table that can be filled incrementally from streamed batches. It estimates entropy, joint and conditional entropy, mutual information and conditional MI over the discrete VQ-VAE codes. It offers both plug-in estimates and bias-corrected Paninski/BUB estimates, which matters because large codebooks make plug-in MI estimates biased upward.
languageLesson: Mutual information I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y) measures how much knowing one code reduces uncertainty about another. With finite samples and many possible symbol pairs, the plug-in estimate overstates I, so bias corrections such as BUB are needed for reliable comparisons.

title: Computing Mutual Information
description: The MI scripts bring all three stages together. For each task, they run a trained GPT (Steps 6-8), quantize its hidden states with trained VQ-VAEs (Steps 9-11), and stream the resulting codes into StreamingInfo (Step 12). mi_calc_minimal.py does this for CFG, mi_calc_full_path.py compares GPT-state codes with Path_VQVAE codes across a full generated path, and NLP_mi_calc_v6 2.py measures MI between per-block and last-token codes on OpenWebText. Comparing these MI values between NTP and MTP models is the project's central experiment.
